en: The Legend of the Elder Paṇṇadāyaka Chapter on the Garland-Worshippers, Number Eight I was once a young brahmin, a student of the Vedas, Living in the city of Benares, devoted to my studies. At that time, the Buddha, the Great Seer, the Teacher of the World, Was dwelling at the foot of the Bodhi tree, having just attained enlightenment. Having completed his meal, the Blessed One, the Great Sage, Set out for Benares, desiring to turn the Wheel of Dhamma. I saw him walking along the road, the Teacher of the World, Radiant with glory, like the sun rising from behind a cloud. Seeing the Buddha, the Great Seer, endowed with all marks of excellence, My heart was filled with joy, and I spoke these words: "O Brahmin youth, you are fortunate indeed! You have seen the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, the Supreme Person. Hearing my words, the Great Seer, the Teacher of the World, Stood still upon the road and addressed me thus: "Young man, what is it that you say? What is the reason for your words? Then I, with palms joined together, spoke these words to the Buddha: "I am a young brahmin, a student of the Vedas, Living in the city of Benares, devoted to my studies. Today I have seen the Blessed One, the Great Seer, The Fully Enlightened One, the Teacher of the World. It is because of this that I speak these words; I am truly fortunate to have seen the Buddha. Then the Buddha, the Great Seer, the Teacher of the World, Spoke these words to me, who stood before him: "Young man, you are fortunate indeed! You have seen the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, the Supreme Person. Having heard the Buddha’s words, I was filled with great joy, And I offered a handful of leaves to the Blessed One. Having made that offering, I took refuge in the Triple Gem, And I set my mind upon the attainment of Buddhahood. For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the lower realms, But always rejoiced among gods and humans. In my final birth, I was born into a wealthy family, And I renounced the world to become a monk under the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa. Having practiced the holy life under the dispensation of Kassapa, I was reborn in the Brahma realm after passing away from here. From there, I passed away and was reborn in the human world, Where I attained parinibbāna in the presence of the Buddha Gotama. By the merit of that offering of leaves, I have been liberated from suffering. May all beings attain such happiness, And may they reach the state of peace, Nibbāna.
"On a mountain in the Himālayas,
I was one who wore garments of bark;
I subsisted on saltless leaves."
And being restrained by my observances,
when the morning meal was ready,
Siddhattha approached me.
With my own hands, full of faith, I gave it to the Buddha.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
Because I gave that leaf at that time,
I do not know any state of misery;
this is the fruit of giving a leaf.
In the twenty-seventh aeon,
I was King Sadatthiya,
endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Paṇṇadāyaka recite these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Paṇṇadāyaka.
